evidence: Quint. 1.7.18: cum in datīvum vel genitīvum cāsum incidissent
terms.comment: Short for cāsus datīvus, the case of giving; Varro and Gellius also say cāsus dandī.

evidence: Varr. LL 8.18; Gell. 4.16.4 (Lewis & Short s.v. datīvus)

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 221, p. 246.
Quintilian checked against the Perseus Latin texts, and cited by its numbering.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
